proposed_section.section_label: Interpretive lenses · Contemplative traditions & philosophy of mind
proposed_section.heading: Ways of describing self and consciousness are not verdicts.

cards.title: Contemplative traditions offer non-ordinary models of selfhood
cards.text: Buddhist non-self analysis and meditation frameworks examine how the sense of self can be constructed, deconstructed and transformed.
cards.boundary: Contemplative phenomenology, tradition and meditation-related changes in self-processing do not establish external ontology or survival after death.

cards.title: Physicalism, dualism and panpsychism remain competing philosophical frameworks
cards.text: These positions offer different accounts of how mind relates to the physical world, but none functions as an empirical verdict on BQ001.
cards.boundary: Philosophical coherence or possibility is not empirical evidence that personal consciousness survives death; physicalism as philosophy is not itself proof of non-survival.

proposed_source_entries: Oxford philosophy chapter on Buddhist non-self; philosophical analysis, not empirical evidence of post-mortem survival.
Peer-reviewed meditation framework concerning cognitive mechanisms of self-processing; not a metaphysical verdict.
Theoretical S-ART framework for mindfulness; psychological self-transcendence does not establish brain-independent consciousness.
Scholarly reference synthesis of physicalist positions; philosophy is not itself proof of non-survival.
Scholarly reference synthesis of dualist positions; conceptual possibility is not evidence that survival occurs.
Scholarly reference synthesis of panpsychist positions; panpsychism does not entail personal survival.
